headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Here’s a quick play‑book so you can pick a short (< 120 min) feature right next door to Times Square:

| Theater | Approximate walk from Times Sq. | How to see the schedule |
|---------|---------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** – 234 W Broadway | ≈ 8–12 min | [amc.com](https://www.amctheatres.com/theaters/new-york-city/amc-empires-25) → “Showtimes” tab |
| **Regal Broadway Cinemas** – 226 W Broadway | ≈ 9–13 min | [regalgoldwynsullivan.com](https://www.regallcinemas.com/) → “Movies & Showtimes” |
| **Alamo Drafthouse Cinema** – 229 W Broadway | ≈ 11–14 min | [drafthouse.com](http://www.drafthouse.com/cinema/alamo-draft-house-cinema-new-york) |
| **Film Forum** – 151 Bleecker St (≈ 20 min walk / subway) | Slightly farther but still doable | [filmforum.org](https://filmforum.org/schedule.html) |

---

### Step‑by‑step guide

1. **Pick a date & time window**  
   *If you’re flexible:* most major chains let you filter by “Today”, “Tomorrow”, or a custom range.  

2. **Filter by runtime**  
   - On AMC’s site, after selecting a theater, click the “Filters” button and tick “Under 2 hrs”.  
   - Reg­al has an advanced search where you can set “Duration ≤ 120 mins.”  
   - For independent venues (e.g., Film Forum), look through the program notes—they usually state runtimes.

3. **Check availability**  
   - Once you’ve narrowed down the title(s), confirm seat inventory. Some shows sell out fast—especially new releases or blockbusters.

4. **Book quickly**  
   - Most theaters accept credit cards online. You’ll get a confirmation email + QR ticket for entry.

---

#### Quick examples (what you’d likely see today)

> *(These are illustrative; actual line‑ups change daily.)*

| Title | Runtime | Theater | Notes |
|-------|--------|---------|------|
| **“Everything Everywhere All At Once”** | 139 min | AMC Empire 25 | Over‑two‑hour, so skip if strict 120‑minute rule. |
| **“Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery”** | 118 min | Regal Broadway | Fits perfectly; comedy‑mystery. |
| **“Spider‑Man: Across the Spider‑Verse”** | 117 min | AMC Empire 25 | Animated superhero, family friendly. |
| **“Past Lives”** | 112 min | Film Forum | Indie drama, great reviews. |
| **“Oppenheimer”** | 155 min | AMC Empire 25 | Too long—skip if you only want < 120 min. |

*(Tip: Many streaming services’ “Now Showing” pages also list runtimes, so you can double‑check before booking.)*

---

### Extra Tips

* **Walk vs. Subway:** Walking takes roughly 10 minutes between Times Square and either AMC or Regal. If you prefer public transit, take the M7 bus southbound or the 42nd Street‑Bryant Park station (B/D/F/M trains) then hop off at 34th Street‑Herald Square and walk east.
* **Food & Drink:** Both AMC and Regal offer concessions inside the lobby. If you want something more upscale, head back toward Times Square for a quick bite—there are plenty of cafés within a minute’s stroll.
* **Special Screenings:** Keep an eye out for midnight premieres or special Q&A events—those often run slightly shorter than standard theatrical cuts.

Let me know if you’d like help narrowing this down further—for instance, picking a particular genre, price point, or even finding a free‑to‑watch option on a streaming platform that matches the same runtime criteria!
